Log-return target formulation
nodes.rationale: TARGET='Close' predicts the price level; for a near-random-walk series the persistence baseline is near-optimal by construction, so the reported -23.5% skill was roughly what the formulation predicts a priori, largely independent of hyperparameters. Modelling r[t]=log(C[t]/C[t-1]) makes the baseline 'predict zero return' (beatable), makes the band scale-free and comparable across symbols, stops GroupNormalizer fighting a non-stationary level, and makes pooling sensible. Measured: skill -59.5% to +2.4% (+3.8% purged) on identical data/seed/epochs. Default deliberately left at 'close' because effective n about 5 is not enough to flip a default and invalidate every existing bundle.

nodes.label: Persistence baseline
nodes.rationale: Predict the last observed close (or zero return under the log-return target). Introduced by PYQ-201 because model quality had been reported only as an absolute QuantileLoss with nothing to compare against; it is the only baseline in the project until PYQ-249 lands.

nodes.label: Walk-forward backtest geometry
nodes.rationale: One 5-day held-out window per symbol is too small and high-variance to drive EarlyStopping and ModelCheckpoint selection; rolling origins with disjoint evaluation windows aggregate PYQ-201's metrics across many origins instead.

nodes.label: Conformalized quantile regression (CQR)
nodes.rationale: Score max(q_lo - y, y - q_hi) on a held-out calibration slice, take the finite-sample corrected quantile ceil((n+1)*coverage)/n, and widen or narrow the band by that amount. Chosen because it is distribution-free, needs no retraining or loss change, is about 80 lines, and composes with the existing quantile head. Only the outer quantiles move: shifting the median would change the reported direction with no evidence for it. The guarantee assumes exchangeability, which financial series violate, so it is paired with purged splits and achieved coverage is reported rather than assumed. Defaults to off (calibration_days=0) because switching it on silently changes every reported coverage figure.

nodes.label: Purge and embargo around splits
nodes.rationale: Lopez de Prado's treatment: drop training samples whose label window overlaps the test window (purge) plus a buffer after it (embargo), because serial correlation leaks across the boundary. The actual leak here is not decoder-to-decoder overlap but that a validation sample's encoder reads max_encoder_length days that are training targets. Measured skill rose rather than fell, which at effective n about 5 is read as inside the noise, establishing only that purging is not catastrophic to fit quality.

nodes.label: Effective sample size under overlapping windows
nodes.rationale: Windows built with min_prediction_idx=cutoff+1 overlap heavily (consecutive windows share 4 of 5 target days), so a raw count of 280 predictions overstates independent evidence by roughly the horizon; a CI computed as if n=280 is about sqrt(5)x too narrow. Reporting effective n is what stopped PYQ-247's ~62-point skill improvement being written up as settled.

nodes.label: Moving-block bootstrap confidence interval
nodes.rationale: Blocks of length at least the horizon preserve the autocorrelation a naive bootstrap destroys, so a directional-accuracy figure can be reported with an interval that answers whether it is distinguishable from 50%.

nodes.label: CRPS (continuous ranked probability score)
nodes.rationale: Strictly proper scoring rule for a full predictive distribution, approximable by averaging pinball loss across quantiles; a single comparable number is what makes a future comparison against a foundation-model baseline meaningful.

nodes.label: Winkler / interval score
nodes.rationale: Scores an interval on coverage AND width in one figure, which is the diagnosis coverage alone structurally cannot give: a band can hit nominal coverage by being enormous. It separated PYQ-247's arms by three orders of magnitude (64.3 vs 0.08). alpha is derived from the configured quantiles rather than assumed 0.2.

nodes.label: PIT histogram
nodes.rationale: Probability-integral transform of actuals through the predictive CDF: uniform means calibrated, U-shaped overconfident, hump-shaped underconfident. Values are computed, aggregated and serialized, but the chart itself is explicitly deferred.

nodes.label: Pinball loss and per-quantile exceedance
nodes.rationale: Outermost-band coverage is the least informative calibration statistic available: it cannot distinguish a calibrated band from one too wide on one side and too narrow on the other. Per-quantile exceedance tells you which side is wrong; pinball loss is the rule the model is actually trained on and is comparable across configs in a way val_loss (reported on normalized targets) is not.

nodes.label: 99.3%-coverage-on-nominal-80% band pathology
nodes.rationale: An 80% band containing 99% of outcomes is useless for decisions and silently collapses scan's band-direction guard into permanent HOLD. Turned out to be substantially a symptom of the non-stationary level target rather than an independent defect.

nodes.label: TTL panel cache and named dataset pins
nodes.rationale: Cache keyed by a fingerprint of (symbol, date range, enabled sources) with a TTL-exempt --pin NAME snapshot that replays byte-identical data later; TTL only gates read validity, so pruning needed its own command.

nodes.label: Provenance block in meta.json / runs.jsonl
nodes.rationale: Records pyquant version, git sha, pin name and resolved config. Not hypothetical: a bug redefined what RSI_14 means, so two bundles with identical feature names can have been trained on different data.

nodes.label: Reproducibility: seed + pinned data + code version
nodes.rationale: Seed alone does not reproduce a run; the missing third leg was code version. Also, seed_everything does not by itself guarantee determinism on every backend (cuDNN autotuning, non-deterministic reductions, num_workers>0 ordering), so the property was tested rather than assumed - it holds exactly on CPU, and GPU determinism is documented as unverified rather than implied.

nodes.label: Pipeline-spanning invariants
nodes.rationale: The backlog was optimising local correctness ticket by ticket while the invariants that span the pipeline went unstated. Six leak bugs were each correct in every individual file and wrong across files, so per-ticket regression tests prevent those three exact recurrences but not the next family member. Stating the invariants once, as properties rather than regressions, makes any future violating change fail regardless of which file it touched.

nodes.label: Learnability test with a degenerate noise control
nodes.rationale: Every existing roundtrip assertion would pass against a model that emits a constant. With a negative headline number there was no way to distinguish 'the target is not forecastable' from 'the wiring is silently broken'. Injecting a known learnable signal discriminates the two in seconds; the white-noise control catches the opposite failure, since a pipeline that finds skill in noise has a leak and this finds it without knowing where.

nodes.label: A tool must earn its place against doing nothing
nodes.rationale: Recurring disposition inherited from the mypy decision: run the tool once, look at what it actually found, then decide whether it is a gate, a local convenience, or a no. Applied to decline MLflow (a 114-line runs.jsonl reader cannot drift from the source of truth and costs no dependencies), to gate ruff D (19 real gaps, zero ongoing maintenance), to defer ruff format as non-blocking, and to skip a fail_under coverage threshold.

nodes.label: Mocking at the transport boundary, not our own function boundary
nodes.rationale: Patching our own fetch_* functions verifies our logic against our own assumptions about the payload, which is half a test - it cannot catch the vendor changing response shape. Recorded real payloads paid for themselves immediately: yfinance returns Dividends/Stock Splits alongside OHLCV, and FRED attaches an entire historical series (26,321 rows) to the earliest vintage boundary. Complementary to the nightly live job: fixtures catch our regressions, the nightly catches theirs.

nodes.label: PriceProvider protocol and vendor abstraction
nodes.rationale: yfinance is an unofficial, unversioned, ToS-ambiguous scraper that is the sole source of OHLCV, VIX, sector ETFs and options - everything degrades gracefully except the one thing everything depends on. Two properties matter more than the vendor chosen: an interface so switching is config not rewrite, and an executable schema contract applied to whatever a provider returns so a subtly different frame fails at the boundary instead of misaligning a join three modules downstream. Tiingo chosen over Alpha Vantage (25 req/day) and Polygon/EODHD (paid), and needs no new dependency.

nodes.label: AUTO_ADJUST price-adjustment convention
nodes.rationale: Whether Close is split/dividend adjusted was decided by whichever yfinance version resolved, and it changes every price level, every derived indicator and therefore every trained model. True is the right convention because an unadjusted series has discontinuities that are not real price moves and every indicator would read them as ones. Stated once as a module constant rather than four files disagreeing.

nodes.label: ALFRED release vintages instead of fixed publication lags
nodes.rationale: A constant publication lag is an approximation in three ways: real release calendars vary, it handles only the first release while macro series are revised (so a 2019 training row sees today's revised number - look-ahead a date shift cannot fix at all), and it needs a hand-maintained constant per series. Vintage retrieval makes the constants unnecessary rather than merely more accurate and generalises to any new series for free.

nodes.label: Structural-missingness indicator columns
nodes.rationale: At period=5y roughly 80% of rows carry a structural Sentiment=0 meaning 'no data', while at prediction time 0 means 'neutral news' - a textbook train/serve distribution shift on a feature, and only the second meaning ever occurs live. The flag marks coverage, not per-day presence: keying it off 'did this row have a headline' would collapse the two meanings the column exists to separate. The same shape of problem recurs for accumulated options history.

nodes.label: Selection-event bias and held-out reporting
nodes.rationale: Every trial in a search is a selection event, so a search of N trials inflates the best observed score; the winning configuration must be reported on a period the search never saw, with the in-search score explicitly labelled optimistically biased. The same caution applies to tuning signal thresholds on the data they are evaluated on.

nodes.label: Bundle feature-schema check
nodes.rationale: Bundles record their feature list and data-config toggles; read-side commands restore those toggles rather than starting from fresh defaults, and doctor turns 'your bundle is broken' from a runtime error into a proactive, deliberately offline check.

nodes.label: Signal P&L evaluation vs. forecast accuracy
nodes.rationale: Accuracy and usefulness are different questions: a model can have excellent MAE and a useless signal (right about magnitude, wrong about the sign that matters), or mediocre MAE and a profitable one. Scored conditional on a signal firing rather than on all days, with turnover and a per-trade cost that is usually decisive at daily frequency. Only informative once the band is calibrated, since the band-direction guard essentially never fires at 99% coverage.

nodes.label: Options snapshot accumulation as a proprietary dataset
nodes.rationale: Put/call ratio, ATM IV and IV skew are the only forward-looking, market-priced signals in the data layer, and they were fetched, printed once and thrown away - because yfinance exposes only a current chain, so no historical IV series can be built from it. Appending a daily snapshot is useless on day one and a genuinely proprietary dataset after a year; the value is time-dependent, which is what makes starting now the highest value-per-effort option. Joined forward-filled with a neutral fill and an indicator rather than the panel's generic ffill+dropna, which would drop nearly the entire training window.

nodes.label: FastAPI service layer additive to the CLI
nodes.rationale: analysis/, models/ and data/ are already fully decoupled from Typer and Rich, so a REST layer is additive rather than a rewrite. Response models are constructed directly from the CLI's own serializers, which makes field-for-field parity true by construction instead of two independently-typed schemas that happen to agree today.

nodes.label: In-process background jobs and where they stop scaling
nodes.rationale: Training blocks for the full fit, so it needs a job model; FastAPI BackgroundTasks plus a status endpoint is enough for a single node, and the stopping point is named explicitly (no queue, no retries, job state lost on restart) as the trigger to move to arq/RQ/Celery + Redis. Local-disk bundles are fine for one instance; multi-instance needs object storage.

nodes.label: Per-bundle lock + LRU bundle cache
nodes.rationale: Serializes predict() against a given loaded model without blocking requests for different bundles, and a bounded LRU cache avoids re-paying checkpoint deserialization and a weights_only=False unpickle per request.

nodes.label: Never make a metric look better without making the model better
nodes.rationale: Applied repeatedly: directional accuracy dropping 80% to 52-56% under the log-return target is reported as the honest number because the old figure was flattered by the formulation; a +36.2% backtest is published beside the -23.5% headline rather than substituted for it because it is not the same measurement; defaults are not flipped on a sample of effective n about 5; acceptance criteria that could not be executed are recorded as verified-in-part rather than claimed whole.

nodes.label: Sphinx + intersphinx chosen over MkDocs
nodes.rationale: The codebase is largely a thin, correct layer over pandas / torch / pytorch-forecasting / pydantic, so resolving upstream types into live links carries real explanatory weight and mkdocstrings does not match intersphinx on this. autodoc_mock_imports was rejected for the same reason: mocked imports silently produce wrong signatures for anything inspecting a base class. A CPU-wheel install (1.2 GB vs 5.2 GB) is the middle path.

nodes.label: Scheduled checks are a notification, not a merge gate
nodes.rationale: A separate workflow beats a continue-on-error step inside CI, because a job in ci.yml appears on every PR's check list even when non-blocking, and a check permanently allowed to be red is a check people stop reading. Live vendor checks assert shape and freshness only, never values; the live smoke test lives inline in the workflow rather than tests/, since a live test in tests/ is one -k away from breaking the offline guarantee.

nodes.label: Time-series foundation model as a third baseline
nodes.rationale: Persistence leaves the central question unanswered: is the TFT - 25 features, four vendors, a training loop, a bundle format - earning its complexity against something that needs none of it? Chronos-2 and TimesFM give probabilistic zero-shot forecasts with no training, features or API key, and all three possible outcomes are informative.

nodes.label: Optuna study over six coupled hyperparameters
nodes.rationale: Learning rate is one of at least six coupled knobs, so tuning it in isolation is close to uninformative. Two prerequisites: land the return target first, or a large search burns GPU hours discovering nothing helps inside a near-unbeatable formulation; and report the winner on a held-out period the search never saw. Two undocumented runtime requirements of pytorch-forecasting's optimize_hyperparameters were recorded inline: it unconditionally builds a TensorBoardLogger and adds a LearningRateMonitor, so tensorboard is required and trainer_kwargs must not set logger=False.

nodes.label: Per-window dispersion beats a mean
nodes.rationale: A mean directional accuracy of 60% built from windows at 100/20/100/40/40 says something very different from five windows at 60%. Only became meaningful once the walk-forward genuinely walked - before that every origin evaluated the same final window and the spread would have reflected model-init noise. Level-target per-window skill [+0.28,+0.47,+0.35,-2.71,-3.13] is the case in point.
